question.text: SEBI can impose a monetary penalty of up to which amount for failure to comply with its directions?

answer.text: Rs. 1 crore or three times the profit made from the violation, whichever is higher

explanation.text: The Logic: The penalty regime in Chapter VIA of the SEBI Act, 1992 includes residuary provisions that allow SEBI to impose monetary penalties for failure to comply with its directions. The widely-cited yardstick is a penalty that may extend to Rs. 1 crore or three times the amount of profit made or loss avoided as a result of the default, whichever is higher. Specific sections in Chapter VIA also prescribe minimum penalty amounts and per-day continuing-default penalties. The Trap: Saying SEBI has no monetary power - only warnings - is incorrect. A flat low cap of Rs. 10 lakh is too narrow and does not match the SEBI Act's "whichever is higher" formulation. A blanket Rs. 25 crore figure is not the general failure-to-comply cap either. Note: The specific Rs. 1 crore-or-three-times-profit formula is not laid out in the cited pages of the NISM-Series-VIII Equity Derivatives workbook, which on the pages checked discusses SEBI powers and exchange/clearing-corporation penalties at a general level. The framing above is general SEBI Act, 1992 penalty knowledge.
